briefs.headline: Leeds beat Tottenham 1-0 on Okafor's late goal, ending a three-match winning run
briefs.summary: Noah Okafor scored in the 79th minute with his first touch, two minutes after coming on, and Leeds outshot Tottenham 16 to five at Elland Road; Mathys Tel went off after Jayden Bogle's studs caught his Achilles, a challenge VAR let stand, and Roberto De Zerbi questioned the officiating. Tottenham drop to 10th on 12 points, below 8th-place Leeds on 14.

briefs.headline: Bengals meet former safety Bates in Madrid with Dugger out
briefs.summary: Jessie Bates III, a Bengal from 2018 to 2022, told ESPN he has not played a playoff game since leaving and that Cincinnati has not been back either; the Bengals, winners of three straight, kick off against Atlanta at 9:30 a.m. ET at the Bernabeu with Kyle Dugger (quadriceps) out and Cedric Johnson (ankle) questionable, and the Falcons without running back Brian Robinson Jr.

briefs.headline: Watson clears protocol, but Sanders starts for the Browns at New Orleans
briefs.summary: Deshaun Watson is out of the concussion protocol and listed questionable, and Todd Monken said Friday that Shedeur Sanders, who won three of seven starts as a rookie, starts at 1 p.m. ET on CBS; the Saints activated rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson, the eighth overall pick, and left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. from injured reserve and released running back Kendre Miller after claiming Audric Estime off waivers from Cleveland.

briefs.headline: Mendez's late goal lifts the Crew past Chicago 4-3 and out of the Wild Card round
briefs.summary: Brais Mendez scored in the third minute of stoppage time after Columbus had trailed three times, Robert Lewandowski converting two first-half penalties for Chicago while Gonzalo Tapia scored twice and Anass Zaroury once for the Columbus Crew; Columbus finish 7th in the East on 47 points, skip the Wild Card round, and open a best-of-three Round One series against Inter Miami.

briefs.headline: Nashville beat FC Cincinnati 2-0 to set an MLS points record
briefs.summary: Sam Surridge scored in the 61st and 86th minutes at TQL Stadium for his 20th and 21st goals, and Nashville finished on 77 points, three past the record Inter Miami set in 2024; FC Cincinnati finished 9th in the East on 46 points, level with Orlando City but behind on wins, and visit Orlando in the Wild Card round on Thursday, Nov. 19, at 7:30 p.m. ET on Apple TV.

briefs.headline: Georgia Southern routs Marshall 49-13 as Johnson throws 4 TD passes
briefs.summary: Max Johnson threw two scoring passes to Jeremiah Ware and ran for another score, Chace Calicut returned an interception 24 yards, and the Eagles scored on four straight drives after halftime in Statesboro; Marshall's touchdowns were runs of 45 yards by Joshon Barbie and 66 by Khalil Wilkins, and the Herd had 412 yards but converted 4 of 13 on third down and turned it over twice. Marshall is 5-4 and 2-3 in the Sun Belt and hosts App State Saturday at 6 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Wembanyama's 29 in 24 minutes carry San Antonio past Portland 125-103
briefs.summary: Victor Wembanyama made 9 of 13 shots, Devin Vassell scored 15 and Stephon Castle and Julian Champagnie 14 each as the Spurs won an eighth straight game and stayed unbeaten in four on the road; Deni Avdija led Portland with 15 and Yang Hansen had his first career double-double. San Antonio, with eight wins and two losses, plays at Phoenix Monday at 9 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Pochettino adds McGlynn to the USMNT roster as Reyna withdraws injured
briefs.summary: U.S. Soccer said Saturday that Stoke City midfielder Jack McGlynn, 23, replaces Gio Reyna, withdrawn with an injury, on the 25-man roster for the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti; McGlynn has 13 caps and a team-high five goals in 11 Championship appearances this season. Training opens Monday in Atlanta, and the first leg is Nov. 14 in Miami at 4:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: No. 13 Texas Tech holds off West Virginia 53-48 after WVU led in the fourth
briefs.summary: Thomas Castellanos threw a career-high five touchdown passes, the last a 5-yarder to Kenny Johnson with 2:44 left, after West Virginia had erased a 14-point halftime deficit and led by seven; the teams combined for 1,220 yards, Michael Hawkins Jr. ran for three scores to reach 19 and tie Ira Errett Rodgers' 1919 school record, and Taron Francis caught three passes for 169 yards. A safety when Hawkins fell in the end zone ended it. WVU is 5-4 and 2-4 in the Big 12 and hosts Kansas Saturday, time not set.

Liverpool are 6th in the Premier League on 15 points from 9 matches (4 wins, 3 draws, 2 losses, GD +2), unchanged, 12 behind leaders Arsenal (27 from 10), per the ESPN eng.1 standings page read at 5:47 a.m. ET Sunday; today's hosts Crystal Palace are 19th on 7 points from 9, two above Sunderland, with Manchester United 18th on 7 from 9 after Saturday's results.

Tottenham are 10th in the Premier League on 12 points from 10 matches (3 wins, 3 draws, 4 losses, GD -1), down one place after Saturday's loss at Leeds, who climbed to 8th on 14; Bournemouth are 9th on 12 from 9 and Newcastle 11th on 12 from 10, per the ESPN eng.1 standings page read at 5:47 a.m. ET Sunday.

The Bengals are 5-2 (W3), 2nd in the AFC North, half a game behind Pittsburgh (6-2, W4) and half a game ahead of Cleveland (5-3), and listed 6th in the AFC, per the ESPN NFL standings page read at 5:47 a.m. ET Sunday, unchanged before today's 9:30 a.m. ET game in Madrid; Baltimore is 4-5. Today's opponent Atlanta is 3-5, 3rd in the NFC South, half a game behind Carolina (3-4).

The Browns are 5-3 (L1), 3rd in the AFC North, one game behind Pittsburgh (6-2) and half a game behind Cincinnati (5-2), with Baltimore (4-5) fourth, and listed 8th in the AFC, per the ESPN NFL standings page read at 5:47 a.m. ET Sunday, unchanged; today's hosts New Orleans are 2-5, at the bottom of the NFC South, one game behind Carolina (3-4).

Columbus finished 7th in the MLS Eastern Conference on 47 points from 34 matches (14 wins, 5 draws, 15 losses, GD +7), up from 8th after Saturday's 4-3 win at Chicago, per the ESPN usa.1 standings page read at 5:47 a.m. ET Sunday; Nashville won the East on 77, Inter Miami, the Crew's Round One opponent, were 2nd on 60, Philadelphia 6th on 50, Orlando 8th on 46 and FC Cincinnati 9th on 46.

FC Cincinnati finished 9th in the MLS Eastern Conference on 46 points from 34 matches (12 wins, 10 draws, 12 losses, GD -8), down from 7th after Saturday's 2-0 home loss to Nashville, level on points with 8th-place Orlando City (13 wins to Cincinnati's 12) and one behind 7th-place Columbus (47), per the ESPN usa.1 standings page read at 5:47 a.m. ET Sunday.

Marshall is 5-4 overall and 2-3 in the Sun Belt (L1), listed 5th of 7 in the Sun Belt East on the ESPN standings page read at 5:47 a.m. ET Sunday, behind James Madison (8-2, 5-2), Georgia Southern (5-4, 4-1) and Georgia State and App State (both 5-4, 2-3); Saturday's visitors App State lost 39-23 to Georgia State.

Ohio is 7-2 overall and 5-0 in the MAC, listed 1st of 13 on the ESPN MAC standings page read at 5:47 a.m. ET Sunday, unchanged with no game Saturday; Toledo (7-2, 4-1) is 2nd, Western Michigan (6-3, 4-1) 3rd and Buffalo (6-3, 4-1) 4th, and Tuesday's hosts Miami (Ohio) are 5-4, 3-2.

The Spurs are 8-2 (W8), listed 2nd in the Western Conference and level with Oklahoma City (8-2, W4) and the Lakers (8-2, W4), per the ESPN NBA standings page read at 5:47 a.m. ET Sunday; Golden State (7-3, W7), Minnesota (7-3) and Houston (7-3) are a game back, Saturday's hosts Portland (6-3) fell to 8th, and Monday's hosts Phoenix (3-5, W2) are 12th.

West Virginia is 5-4 overall and 2-4 in the Big 12 (L1), listed 10th of 16 on the ESPN Big 12 standings page read at 5:47 a.m. ET Sunday, down from 8th after Saturday's loss at Texas Tech; Utah leads at 9-0 (6-0) after beating BYU, Texas Tech is 2nd at 8-1 (5-1), BYU (7-2, 4-2) 3rd and Houston (7-2, 4-2) 4th, and Saturday's visitors Kansas are 3-6 and 16th.

briefs.headline: Yoshinofuji beats yokozuna Onosato on day 1 of the Kyushu basho
briefs.summary: Komusubi (the fourth-highest rank) Yoshinofuji, the Kumamoto-born local favorite, thrust down yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato in 3.2 seconds in the final bout at the Fukuoka Kokusai Center, a result the judges upheld after a mono-ii (judges' conference) over whether Onosato's hand or Yoshinofuji's foot touched down first; it was the first bout for the new tate-gyoji (chief referee), the 40th Kimura Shonosuke, who said Yoshinofuji's foot had stayed in. Yoshinofuji has won five of six against Onosato.

briefs.headline: Hoshoryu wins his return bout, pushing out Churanoumi in 7.8 seconds
briefs.summary: Yokozuna Hoshoryu, back after three straight tournaments with absences following right knee surgery, beat new komusubi Churanoumi by oshidashi (push out) after absorbing a throat push, his seventh win in seven meetings; he said he was a little relieved and that it was not good sumo but he was glad to win. He meets maegashira (rank-and-file) 1 Asanoyama on day 2, having won all five previous bouts between them.

briefs.headline: Ozeki Aonishiki and Kotozakura both lose on day 1; Wakatakakage wins juryo return
briefs.summary: Maegashira 1 Asanoyama forced down ozeki (champion, the second-highest rank) Aonishiki and Fujiryoga pushed out ozeki Kotozakura, while ozeki Kirishima beat Ura and sekiwake Fujinokawa lost to Fujiseiun, per Nikkan Sports' bout-by-bout results; in juryo (the second division), Wakatakakage, down from the top division after four leg operations, beat Ryuden by yorikiri (force out), and Shirokuma withdrew with a right ankle ligament injury, the first kyujo (absence) in the top two divisions.

briefs.headline: No. 4 Notre Dame beats No. 1 Miami 31-24 after leading by 21
briefs.summary: CJ Carr threw for 319 yards and three touchdowns, two to Micah Gilbert, and the Irish (8-1) led 24-3 early in the third quarter before Darian Mensah's three scoring passes twice brought Miami (8-1) within seven; a fourth-down catch by Elija Lofton in the end zone with 3:36 left was ruled incomplete when Luke Talich knocked the ball away, a call Mario Cristobal said left him "beyond upset." Georgia may take the top spot when the CFP rankings come out Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Stockton's 4 TD passes carry No. 2 Georgia past Ole Miss 42-7 in Oxford
briefs.summary: Georgia (8-1, 6-1 SEC) scored touchdowns on its first four possessions for a 28-0 halftime lead, snapping Ole Miss's 16-game home winning streak; Trinidad Chambliss, who accounted for five scores against Georgia last season, was 18 of 34 for 170 yards, was sacked five times and went without a touchdown pass for the first time in 22 games. Kirby Smart won in Oxford for the first time in three tries, and the Rebels, 10th in the CFP rankings, fell to 6-3.

briefs.headline: No. 3 Utah stays unbeaten, beating No. 9 BYU 28-20 on four interceptions
briefs.summary: Devon Dampier threw two touchdown passes to Braden Pegan and ran for two scores, and Utah (9-0, 6-0 Big 12) intercepted Bear Bachmeier four times, twice in the end zone in the fourth quarter, to end a three-game losing run in the rivalry; BYU (7-2, 4-2) led 20-14 at halftime and did not score after it. Utah and Texas Tech are the Big 12's top two.

briefs.headline: Curry scores 41 as the Warriors beat Orlando 126-119 in OT for a seventh straight
briefs.summary: Stephen Curry converted a three-point play with 1:38 left in overtime and a layup in the final minute, his 16th 40-point game since turning 35, passing LeBron James' 15 for the most in NBA history, and became the seventh player with 26,000 points, 5,000 rebounds and 6,000 assists; Golden State, which opened the season with three losses, has its longest streak since March 2025. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 23 points, and Franz Wagner 30 points and 11 assists for the Magic.

briefs.headline: Thunder hold the Wizards to 75, the NBA's lowest total this season, in a 114-75 rout
briefs.summary: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 30 in three quarters and sat out the fourth, rookie Aday Mara had 18 points, eight rebounds and three blocks, and Washington shot 29 of 98 and 7 of 43 from three without Anthony Davis; Oklahoma City, with eight wins and two losses, has won five of seven since losing Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Chet Holmgren to long-term injuries.

briefs.headline: Brunson's 18 straight points carry the Knicks past the Cavaliers 109-97
briefs.summary: Jalen Brunson scored 31 with nine assists, including 18 in a row over 4:24 of the second quarter, and Karl-Anthony Towns added 29 in the first meeting since the defending champions swept Cleveland in last season's Eastern Conference finals; Donovan Mitchell scored 21 of his season-high 37 in the fourth quarter for the Cavaliers, who were without Jarrett Allen.

briefs.headline: Crosby passes Dionne for 6th on the NHL scoring list in a 5-2 Penguins win
briefs.summary: Sidney Crosby, 39, scored twice at Los Angeles, his 1,772nd point coming when Evgeni Malkin's one-timer deflected in off him in the second period, and added an empty-netter while diving face-first; Tommy Novak scored twice in the first six minutes and Pittsburgh snapped a four-game losing streak with its third win in 11 games.

briefs.headline: Hurricanes score 9 on the Blackhawks, tying a Carolina record
briefs.summary: Jordan Martinook and Andrei Svechnikov scored twice each and seven players scored for the NHL-best Hurricanes, who have outscored their last two visitors 16-2 and won six of seven; Spencer Knight was pulled after six goals on 17 shots, and Chicago has lost six straight. Alexander Nikishin, unsigned when the season began, scored in his season debut.

briefs.headline: Kucherov's overtime goal lifts the Lightning past the Wild 4-3
briefs.summary: Nikita Kucherov, who has asked Tampa Bay for a trade over what he called a lack of communication from general manager Julien BriseBois, scored on a power play 3:23 into overtime for his first goal in seven games after the Lightning erased a 3-1 third-period deficit; Jake Guentzel had two goals and an assist. Minnesota, which leads the Western Conference with 28 points, had won three straight.

briefs.headline: Colts take trade calls on Daniel Jones ahead of Tuesday's deadline, sources say
briefs.summary: Indianapolis has received calls from multiple teams about Jones, who starts today against Dallas, and is willing to listen through the 4 p.m. ET deadline Tuesday, league sources told ESPN and NFL Network; Baltimore checked in before trading for Jacoby Brissett, and Jones carries a $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027 that becomes fully guaranteed March 15 if he stays on the roster.

briefs.headline: Ravens tell Henry he is not being traded, sources say
briefs.summary: Baltimore informed Derrick Henry it has no intention of dealing him before Tuesday's deadline and never considered it, league sources told ESPN, after speculation tied to the loss of Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injury; the one Ravens running back the Giants asked about was Justice Hill. Henry said he has not raised a move: "Let's go back to work."

briefs.headline: Hall of Famer Jack Ham hospitalized in stable condition after a medical emergency
briefs.summary: Ham, 77, the Penn State radio analyst and four-time Super Bowl champion with the Steelers, was taken to the University of Washington Medical Center during Penn State's win at Washington on Saturday, coach Matt Campbell said, crediting play-by-play partner Steve Jones with a "heroic effort" in helping him; Ham entered the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1988.

briefs.headline: Delap's two goals beat Manchester City 3-1, a third straight league loss for City
briefs.summary: Jair Cunha robbed Josko Gvardiol for the sixth-minute opener and Liam Delap, who had scored once in eight games since his club-record move from Chelsea, struck in the 19th and 73rd minutes at the City Ground for Nottingham Forest's first home league win since April; Rayan Cherki pulled one back in the 52nd. City stay 2nd, six points behind Arsenal, and the result dropped Manchester United into the bottom three.

briefs.headline: Manchester United end a day in the relegation zone for the first time in 40 years
briefs.summary: Forest's win over City left United 18th on 7 points after nine matches, the first time since November 1986 they have ended a day in the bottom three this deep into a season; Michael Carrick's side, winless in the league since Aug. 30, host Aston Villa today at 11:30 a.m. ET and would start the match bottom if Sunderland beat Chelsea and Crystal Palace avoid defeat against Liverpool at 9 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Odegaard's late goal beats Hull 1-0 and sends Arsenal into the break six clear
briefs.summary: Martin Odegaard tucked in a rebound in the 72nd minute for a seventh straight home win, after referee Farai Hallam, sent to the monitor on a shirt-pull by Nobel Mendy on Kai Havertz, ruled Havertz offside and gave Hull a free kick, though the report noted the laws say the foul should take precedence when the player is not playing the ball; Arsenal have 27 points from 10 matches to Manchester City's 21.

briefs.headline: Messi wins a second straight Golden Boot with 26 goals, an MLS first
briefs.summary: Lionel Messi, 39, finished four clear of FC Dallas' Petar Musa with 26 goals in 31 games and added a league-high 17 assists, though Inter Miami surrendered a three-goal halftime lead and drew with Charlotte on the final day; Miami held 2nd in the East and open Round One against Columbus. Sam Surridge of Nashville was third with 21.

briefs.headline: Real Salt Lake beat the Galaxy 2-1 for the West's last playoff place
briefs.summary: Sergi Solans and rookie Zach Booth scored in the 10th and 13th minutes in Sandy, Utah, and Real Salt Lake, which had a 13-game winless run in midseason, made the playoffs for a fifth straight year while the Galaxy missed the postseason for a second straight season after winning MLS Cup in 2024; RSL visit Seattle in the Wild Card round Thursday, Nov. 19, at 10 p.m. ET, the winner facing Vancouver.

briefs.headline: Sullivan brothers score as Philadelphia beat Toronto 4-1 to clinch Round One
briefs.summary: Cavan Sullivan, 17, scored twice and Quinn Sullivan had a goal and two assists at Subaru Park, the third brother pair to score for the same club in one MLS match; Cavan's 23 goal contributions are a record for a teenager in a regular season, and the Union, 6th in the East on 50 points, open a best-of-three against New England.

briefs.headline: Taiwanese closer Tseng enters MLB's posting system before a likely lockout
briefs.summary: Jyun-Yue Tseng, a 25-year-old right-hander with 25 saves for the Fubon Guardians this year, can sign with any club from today until Dec. 22, the AP reported; the posting fee is 20% of the first $25 million of a major league contract, and MLB is likely to lock out the players when the collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1, which could cut the window short.

Saturday, Nov. 7, was the pamphlet table's biggest opening day of the fall: bobwhite quail through Jan. 2, daily bag three, possession nine, closed on Tomblin WMA; cottontail rabbit through Feb. 28, daily bag five, possession 20; snowshoe or varying hare through Feb. 28, daily bag two, possession eight; ring-necked pheasant, cock birds only, through Jan. 2, daily bag two, possession two; raccoon trapping, and red and gray fox hunting and trapping, through Feb. 28; bobcat hunting and trapping through Feb. 28, season limit three, electronic registration required; and the trapping lines for mink and muskrat, and for skunk, opossum, coyote and weasel, through Feb. 28, fisher through Jan. 31 and otter through Feb. 28 at a season limit of one each with registration, and beaver through March 31 with registration. prime.method: Second segment of a three-way split
prime.dates: Oct. 3 to 11, Nov. 7 to 15, Dec. 21 to Jan. 31
prime.item: Day 2 of 9. The duck table's second segment opened Saturday, Nov. 7, and closes Sunday, Nov. 15, seven days out, with the third segment Dec. 21 through Jan. 31; the first, Oct. 3 to 11, is closed, and both youth waterfowl days, Sept. 19 and Oct. 31, are past. The migratory summary's duck line reads daily bag six, possession 18, with the sub-limits in footnote (c): no more than four mallards, two of them hens, two black ducks, three pintails, three wood ducks, two redheads, two canvasbacks and four sea ducks, no more than three scoters and three long-tailed ducks among them; scaup, inside the duck bag, reads one per day Nov. 7 to 15 and Dec. 21 to Jan. 11 and two per day Jan. 12 to 31; coots run the same dates as ducks at 15 and 45, mergansers the same dates at five and 15 in aggregate. Canada and white-fronted geese and snow and blue geese share the Nov. 7 to 15 segment and a third Dec. 8 through Jan. 31, daily bag five and possession 15 in aggregate; brant open Jan. 2 at one and three. Shooting hours for waterfowl are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset, and HIP registration is required. The dates are not in the hunting and trapping pamphlet, which says so itself; they were re-read this morning from WVDNR's separate Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary 2026-2027, which fetched through the proxy at 5:45 a.m. (HTTP 200, 1,940,942 bytes, md5 aad32d21343547146e3977a821a39355, byte-identical to Saturday's copy, a 23rd straight morning).

The dove season's second segment opened Monday, Nov. 2, and closes Sunday, Nov. 15, seven days out, the same day the duck and goose second segments and the fall turkey window close; the third segment is Dec. 7 through Jan. 10. The migratory summary's line reads daily bag 15, possession 45, and its shooting-hours paragraph puts dove hours at one-half hour before sunrise to sunset for every day but the first segment's opener. The dates are not in the hunting and trapping pamphlet, which says so itself; they were re-read this morning from WVDNR's separate Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary 2026-2027, which fetched through the proxy at 5:45 a.m. (HTTP 200, 1,940,942 bytes, md5 aad32d21343547146e3977a821a39355, byte-identical to Saturday's copy, a 23rd straight morning).

Day 14 of 21. The fall turkey window of Oct. 26 through Nov. 15 is open in the 14 counties the pamphlet's page 41 lists under that column: Berkeley, Grant, Greenbrier, Hampshire, Hardy, Mineral, Monroe, Morgan, Nicholas, Pendleton, Pocahontas, Randolph, Tucker and Webster, the cabin county among them; the Oct. 26 to Nov. 1 column, which included Mason, Putnam and Wood, closed Nov. 1, and the Oct. 10 to 18 column, which included Cabell, Kanawha and Summers, closed last month. Page 41 reads one either-sex turkey for the whole fall season by bow, crossbow or gun, electronic registration required, dogs legal, shooting hours one-half hour before sunrise to one-half hour after sunset; the 14-county column was read again this morning from page 45 of the pamphlet PDF (HTTP 200, 7,606,482 bytes, md5 ff6261bef172f4d0ab748ce930260fd2, unchanged). The pamphlet is valid through June 30, 2027, checked against this morning's date.

waters.reading: 52.4 cfs, 1.32 feet at 5:15 a.m., falling on flow against 56.2 cfs and steady on stage against 1.35 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.working: Against Saturday's edition reading of 57.5 cfs and 1.36 feet at 5:15 a.m. the gauge is down 5.1 cfs and 0.04 feet on the day, and Friday's bump is gone: the USGS record came off 57.5 at 2:30 a.m. Saturday to 56.2 at 5:45, flickered between 54.9 and 56.2 from 10:30 a.m. to 12:45 p.m., settled at 54.9 through the afternoon, dropped to 53.7 at 6:15 p.m. and to 52.4 at 2:45 a.m. Sunday, with one 15-minute return to 53.7 at 3:15; the stage went 1.36, 1.35, 1.34, 1.33, 1.32 on the same steps. The daily mean for Saturday was 55.7 cfs against 58.8 Friday and 55.6 Thursday, so the two-day rise was a shower on the headwaters or a cloud over the gauge's sun, and the recession has resumed from a new floor: 52.4 is the lowest reading of the fall, under Thursday's 54.9, on a slide that ran from 1,360 cfs on Oct. 15 through 653 on Oct. 17, 141 on Oct. 24 and 70.7 on Oct. 31. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, printed as it stands, "52 cfs - prime wading water." Stocking: WVDNR's fish-stocking page, fetched this morning, again carries an empty list under the waters stocked, and the river's most recent stocking this paper has reported is still Oct. 29. At 52 cfs and clear the Williams is the file's low-water problem at its lowest yet: pocket water and plunge pools shrunk to their cores, every fish in the deepest slot of each pocket, the water cold and glass-clear, and a wading angler the loudest thing on the river. Structure is pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks; forage is caddis, stoneflies and sculpin. So: a long leader, nine to 12 feet to 6X or 7X, and small flies, a size 16 to 18 caddis pupa or a size 18 soft-hackle swung into the plunge-pool tailouts, a size 16 to 18 pheasant tail or small black stonefly nymph under a tiny indicator or a dry-dropper through the pocket seams, a size 20 to 22 blue-winged olive on top through the middle of an overcast day, and for the one bigger fish in each plunge pool a size 8 to 10 olive or black sculpin pattern fished on a short line into the foam at the head of the pool at first or last light, before the sun gets on it; an egg pattern or a San Juan worm under a small indicator still covers the holdover stocked pools. The heavy-nymph-on-the-seam game is for 500 cfs, a number this river has not seen since the 653 of Oct. 17.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.55 feet at 5 a.m., falling against 24.97 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 24.6 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Against Saturday's edition reading of 24.95 at 5 a.m. the pool is down 0.40 on the day, the steadiest day of drawdown this week: the trace held between 24.74 and 24.95 through Saturday morning and afternoon, touched 24.95 again at 4 p.m., dropped to 24.65 at 6 p.m., ran 24.63 to 24.79 through the evening, eased through the 24.6s overnight and reached 24.55 at 5 a.m. Sunday, with none of the quarter-hour jumps that marked Saturday's dawn. No rain in the bucket, so this is the dam letting the pool down, not the hills. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 24.6 the gauge is two and a half feet under the up-and-pushing line at 27. A pool dropping four-tenths in a day still fishes the structure, not the slack: wing dams, riprap and the lock wall are the file's structure, shad and skipjack with crawfish in the rock the forage. A white or pearl three-and-a-half to four-inch swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-quarter-ounce spoon down the current face of each wing dam at first light for hybrids and white bass; a crawfish-colored jig or a three-inch tube dragged slow on the riprap through the day for smallmouth and drum; and with the water cooling into November a half-ounce blade bait or a jig and minnow worked vertical along the lock wall seam and the barge-cut edges for sauger, cut skipjack on the bottom in the cuts after dark for blue catfish. A falling pool pulls the shad off the flats and onto the wing-dam faces, which puts the first hour of light on the rock.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.04 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 26.17 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.0 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Against Saturday's edition reading of 26.19 at 5 a.m. the gauge is down 0.15 on the day, and the day in between was the sawtooth and nothing else: the trace swung between 25.95 and 26.36 every quarter hour from Saturday dawn to Sunday dawn, the high at 11:15 p.m. and the low at 9:45 p.m., with no sustained climb like Friday's and no drain like Thursday night's. The dam below tells the rest: the USGS gauge at Ironton, Ohio, below Greenup Dam, recorded Greenup's discharge at 22,500 cfs at 5 a.m. Saturday, between 24,200 and 29,100 on the hourly readings through the day, 28,200 at 6 and 7 p.m., then down to 21,600 at 9 p.m., 18,900 at 2 and 3 a.m. and 22,000 at 5 a.m. Sunday, the Ironton stage 34.41 to 34.28 over the same day. So Greenup passed its usual daytime water and cut back overnight, and the Huntington reach held within four-tenths of a foot through all of it while the Byrd pool above came down four-tenths; whether the drawdown above is scheduled for the week or a lockage rhythm the traces still do not say, and this paper will not guess. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access. Below the dam the reach is a tenth and a half under Saturday morning with Greenup drawing 22,000 cfs below, so there is a little less push on the seams than Saturday and the fishing still goes to them: a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon down the current face of the wing dams at first light for hybrids and white bass, a half-ounce blade bait or a chartreuse-and-white paddletail on a half-ounce head worked slow along the lock wall's downstream edge for sauger, a crawfish jig on the riprap at midday, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the slack beside the discharge after dark for blue and flathead catfish. No color in either trace; the slack-behind-the-dams game is for a muddy river, not this one.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 12:57 AM at 0.3 ft, high 7:05 AM at 4.3 ft, low 1:44 PM at 0.6 ft, high 7:19 PM at 3.5 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 11:47 PM (Sat) at 0.2 ft, high 6:20 AM at 5.5 ft, low 12:43 PM at 0.3 ft, high 6:36 PM at 4.1 ft. Water 66.7F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:36 a.m. Moon a waning crescent, 2% illuminated, 28.1 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 7:05 AM and 7:19 PM in the sound.
waters.working: All four of the sound's events land inside the calendar day again, the 12:57 a.m. low behind us at press time, while the surf table's first event is Saturday night's 11:47 p.m. low, tagged so nobody reads it as tonight's; the sound lags the surf 45 minutes on the morning high, 61 on the midday low and 43 on the evening high, the long-lag-on-the-ebb pattern the reference describes. The ranges are the biggest of the week and still building: a 4.0-foot fill overnight from 0.3 to this morning's 4.3, a 3.7-foot drain to 1:44 p.m., a 2.9-foot fill to 7:19 p.m., the morning sound high 4.3 against Saturday's 4.2 and the surf high 5.5 against 5.4, with the moon at 2% and the new moon about Monday, so these are spring tides at their peak and the inlet will run hard either side of slack. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, reads 66.7F, down 1.5 on Saturday's 68.2 and the first cooling after four warming mornings. What's running: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report for November, published Sunday, Nov. 1, is seven days old this morning, a monthly report and not today's conditions. It has the Jolly Roger Pier with scattered speckled trout starting to show, night bottom fishing producing Virginia mullet and spot, and bluefish thick in the early mornings; Surf City Pier with pompano, black drum and croaker on the bottom, casting shots at Spanish and bluefish, and king mackerel good before the last blow; East Coast Sports with the piers catching big red drum of 32 inches and more, mostly on the north end, smaller reds and the occasional trout inside, a few trout in the surf, and trout to dominate as it cools; Native Son with cooling water pushing trout into the creeks, the five- to eight-foot seams the depth to look, reds inside taking cut bait, and false albacore possible for sight-casters; Capt. Ricky Kellum with many small specks and some to 28 inches on live shrimp under a cork in four to eight feet of water, black drum to 18 inches and small reds on the same floated shrimp, and a 3/16-ounce jighead with a soft plastic for the artificial; Carolina Flats with topwater early to find the trout schools, deeper holes later, and reds on the oyster and grass banks on soft plastics before the bait thins; and the boats with kings in 50 to 60 feet, bluefish, false albacore and gray trout on the nearshore structure, sea bass and triggerfish on the bottom in 60 to 80 feet. Beach conditions: no NWS Wilmington product was active for coastal Pender or Onslow, the Topsail point or the adjacent marine zones at 5:46 a.m.; the only North Carolina product on the wire was a Frost Advisory for Piedmont counties to 9 a.m. Tide is the whole game, and this morning it is the top of the flood at press time: the sound fills to 4.3 at 7:05 a.m. and then drains for six and a half hours to the 1:44 p.m. low, the biggest morning ebb of the week on the new-moon tide. Structure here is oyster bars, grass edges, dock lights and the ICWW channel, forage mud minnows, shrimp and finger mullet, which is the report's live-shrimp-and-small-plastic fishing. Trout first: a topwater plug over the flooded grass edges in the first hour of light around the 7:05 a.m. high, then a 3/16- or quarter-ounce jighead with a paddletail or soft jerkbait worked slow down the five- to eight-foot seams where the creek channels drop into the ICWW as the drain gathers through mid-morning, and a popping cork with live shrimp over the oyster bars on the first of the flood after 2 p.m. and again either side of the 7:19 p.m. high; with the water at Beaufort under 67F the trout move to the deeper holes on the midday low. Red drum want the last of the fall, which on this table is roughly 11:15 a.m. to the 1:44 p.m. low, cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a quarter-ounce head a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges as the grass drains; the dusk high at 7:19 p.m. puts drum up on the flooded grass and oyster banks for a weedless gold spoon or a soft plastic, and the ebb that follows runs under the dock lights past midnight, the report's small plastics or a suspending twitchbait where the shrimp and finger mullet stack. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel an hour either side of the evening high. Bluefish are the early-morning fish on the beach behind the bait pods on a metal jig or topwater, per both piers. Flounder are release only.
